note.text:
This practical needs a microscope; here you learn the steps.
Onion cells (plant):
1. Peel a thin layer of skin from inside an onion scale.
2. Lay it flat in a drop of water on a slide.
3. Add a drop of iodine solution to stain it.
4. Lower a cover slip slowly at an angle, to avoid air bubbles.
5. Look under low power, then high power.
You see box-shaped cells side by side, each with a cell wall and a nucleus. Onion skin has no chloroplasts: it is not green.
Cheek cells (animal): gently scrape the inside of your own cheek with a clean cotton bud, smear it on a slide, add a drop of methylene blue stain and a cover slip. You see flat, rounded cells with a nucleus and no wall. Put the used bud in the bin at once.

worked_example.problem: Why is the cover slip lowered slowly at an angle?
steps: Air bubbles look like round shapes and can be mistaken for cells.
Lowering it at an angle pushes the air out.

cards.idea: To see onion cells: thin skin, a drop of water, iodine stain, a cover slip lowered at an angle, then the microscope.
example: A stain makes the nucleus and wall easier to see.

cards.idea: Onion cells look like boxes with walls; cheek cells are rounder with no wall.
Stains such as iodine (plants) and methylene blue (cheek cells) make cell parts easier to see.
example: Without a stain the cells are almost clear.

check.prompt: Why is a stain such as iodine added to the slide?

right.text: to make the cell parts easier to see

wrong.text: to kill germs on the slide
wrong.explain: Its job here is to colour the cells so they show.
A stain colours; the microscope magnifies.
The water holds the cover slip; the stain colours.
The stain only colours the cells.

pick.t: box-shaped cells with walls, side by side
pick.why: Onion cells: box-shaped cells with walls, side by side.

pick.t: flat, rounded cells with no wall
pick.why: Cheek cells: flat, rounded cells with no wall.
Onion cells: cells stained with iodine.
Cheek cells: cells stained with methylene blue.

misconceptions.explain: Plant cells have walls; animal cells do not.

questions.prompt: Why is the cover slip lowered slowly at an angle?

wrong.explain: It only pushes the air out.

wrong.text: to make the image upside down

questions.prompt: Why are there no chloroplasts in onion skin cells?

right.text: The onion bulb grows under the ground, away from light, so it is not green.

wrong.explain: There were none: the bulb is not green.

wrong.text: Chloroplasts are only in animal cells.
wrong.explain: Chloroplasts are only in plant cells, in green parts.
In green leaves they are easy to see.

right.text: A used cotton bud goes straight in the bin.
Iodine helps to show onion cells.
